questions.key_step: Corner triangle area is constant so alpha*beta=4, mid-point gives xy=1
questions.justification: One standard idea (constant intercept-triangle area gives a rectangular hyperbola), three short lines.

questions.key_step: Centroid = incentre so r is the distance to the side; R=2r
questions.justification: Direct formula for an equilateral triangle; essentially one result applied once.

questions.key_step: Chord condition g^2-c=4a^2 plus point condition, eliminate c
questions.justification: Routine two-condition elimination on the general circle, then recognising the conic.

questions.key_step: m=1 from the perpendicular tangent; distance of centre = radius
questions.justification: Tangent at a point, perpendicular slope, tangency distance: all one-step standard results.

questions.key_step: Intercepts 7/cos and 7/sin; eliminate theta; sign from quadrant
questions.justification: Parametric mid-point locus and elimination of theta; standard but needs the quadrant check.

questions.key_step: Perpendicular gives beta=2alpha; area gives AB^2*AC^2=500; quadrant picks sign
questions.justification: Three linked standard steps with a sign decision at the end.

questions.key_step: Angle formula with equal tangents (or compute side lengths)
questions.justification: Quick identification of the triangle type; vertices are integers.

questions.key_step: Normal through the centre, tangent perpendicular; base AB, height 7
questions.justification: Tangent and normal equations, two intercepts and an area; precise arithmetic with fractions.

questions.key_step: Diagonals bisect: two linear equations
questions.justification: Standard parallelogram relation plus a 2x2 linear system.

questions.key_step: Concurrent case by determinant, two parallel cases; floor of 32.64
questions.justification: Two mechanisms for 'no triangle' must be listed; small precision risk.

questions.key_step: Slope-form tangent with distance = radius gives m^2=1/8; PQ via foot of perpendicular
questions.justification: Two curves, a common-tangent condition and a foot-of-perpendicular computation; numerical so no option check.

questions.key_step: Slopes 1 and -3/4 from P; choose signs for positive intercepts; intersect
questions.justification: Tangents from a point, sign selection for positive intercepts, then a second intersection; several places to slip.

questions.key_step: Chord of contact equals the given line; compare coefficients
questions.justification: Pole-polar with a three-ratio comparison; short once the idea is seen.

questions.key_step: a^2=16, e=1/2 from focus and directrix; tangent through (0,4 sqrt3) gives theta=30
questions.justification: Focus-directrix, parametric tangent and a distance: standard chain of three steps.

questions.key_step: a-2b+c=0 gives P(1,-2); Delta=0 for the system gives alpha, beta
questions.justification: Two chapters joined in one line each; routine determinants.

questions.key_step: Equate normal slope with the slope to (0,3/2); x1 cancels, y1=1
questions.justification: Implicit differentiation and a clean cancellation; routine.

questions.key_step: Base angles 30 degrees give B(3,0); line BC; beta^4/alpha^2 simplifies to 36
questions.justification: Trigonometric set-up, surd simplification at the end; precise but standard.

questions.key_step: Reflect B in y=4 for the minimum; convexity puts the maximum at an end-point
questions.justification: Reflection trick is familiar, but the maximum needs a separate argument that the PDF skips.

questions.key_step: Parametric normal slope -2 sin(theta) = -sqrt2 gives theta=pi/4
questions.justification: Standard hyperbola normal formula and a distance; short.

questions.key_step: Centre equidistant from x=3 and y=2 gives alpha=3/2
questions.justification: Single equation |alpha|=|alpha-3|; one familiar move.
